title: Triangle BVH for fast raycasts
purpose: Build a bounding volume hierarchy over a triangle mesh or BufferGeometry with binned surface area heuristic splits in flat typed arrays, then cast closest-hit rays (distance, triangle, barycentrics, point) and early-out any-hit rays with side culling. Use it for picking, shooting and line of sight.

engine.name: node
engine.notes: No three.js needed: it reads typed arrays or a BufferGeometry's position and index arrays. The demo was rendered with three.js 0.186.1 in headless Chrome.

exports.name: buildTriangleBVH
exports.summary: The hierarchy as typed arrays: nodeBounds, nodeOffsets, nodeCounts and the triangle order.

exports.name: bvhFromGeometry
exports.summary: The same from a BufferGeometry's position attribute and index.

exports.name: raycastBVH
exports.signature: raycastBVH(bvh, origin, direction, options = {}) -> {distance, triangle, barycentric, point} | null
exports.summary: Closest hit between near and far, nearest child first.

exports.summary: Whether anything is hit; stops at the first hit.

options.meaning: Leaves at or under this size are not split.

options.meaning: Centroid bins per axis for the surface area heuristic.

limits: Static meshes: the hierarchy references the position and index arrays, so after editing or animating vertices you must build again; skinned and morphed meshes are not followed. Rays are in the geometry's local space: transform them by the inverse of the object's world matrix yourself. Hits exactly on a shared edge may report either triangle. Building is single-threaded in O(n log n) and holds float64 boxes (48 bytes per node). No ray packets, no closest-point queries and no mesh-mesh collision. Only three.js 0.186.1 was run for the demo, in headless Chrome on SwiftShader WebGL 2.
